componentPlan.focusQuote: On the Moon g is about 1.62 m/s^2, roughly one sixth of the 9.8 m/s^2 we feel on Earth.

overview.headline: Moon throws fly ballistic without drag under low gravity

keyPoints.point: A thrown ball on the Moon flies ballistic with no drag because there is no air.
keyPoints.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all.

keyPoints.point: Horizontal speed stays steady through flight because nothing pushes the ball sideways.
keyPoints.quote: Nothing pushes the ball sideways, so the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight

keyPoints.point: Gravity slows vertical motion at a steady rate and changes speed over time.
keyPoints.quote: Vertically, gravity slows the ball at a steady rate g.

keyPoints.point: The ball stops rising at the highest point predicted by the height equation.
keyPoints.quote: The ball stops rising when V = 0, which happens at t = V0 / g.

keyTerms.gloss: resistance from air that would slow a thrown ball
keyTerms.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all.

keyTerms.gloss: flight with no drag after launch pulled only by weight
downward force that pulls the ball straight down
keyTerms.quote: The only force on the ball after it leaves the hand is its weight, which pulls it straight down.

keyTerms.gloss: sideways speed that stays steady during flight
keyTerms.quote: Nothing pushes the ball sideways, so the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight

keyTerms.gloss: upward speed that changes over time during flight
keyTerms.quote: The vertical speed is V = V0 - g * t, and the height is y = V0 * t - g * t^2 / 2.

analysis.pageCoverage: Explains drag free ballistic flight on the Moon, splitting launch velocity into steady horizontal motion and gravity slowed vertical motion leading to peak height.
